Home / Museum Ship Reports / Museo Maritomo Nacional, Valparaiso

Date visited 19 April 2024

Today's visit was to the Museo Maritimo Nacional, in Valparaiso, Chile.

Valparaiso is about 1.5 hrs drive from the capital, Santiago, and there is a very good bus service between the two cities, so this museum is easily visitable as a day trip on public transport from Santiago.

The museum is located on the top of a hill overlooking the naval base.  The Museum building itself is a historic artifact - I think it might have been the fleet headquarters or something like that in the past.  The view of the base would have made it a great place for taking photographs (there were six frigates in port today - plus a number of other vessels) - if only there hadn't been a container terminal between the base and the museum which cluttered the view (see photo below)The museum is really well presented, the galleries are well organised, captions aren't extensive - but they are generally bi-lingual.  It has all the things you would expect to see in a national naval museum - photos, models, artefacts, guns, torpedos, mines, models, dioramas, etc.  Out the front they have an armoured conning tower - not sure which ship it was from, but it looked like something you might see on a turn of the (last) century cruiser - along with two British-built 3-inch guns in superb condition.

Not surprisingly there was a strong emphasis in the museum on the War of the Pacific, and the various actions the Chilean Navy was involved in in the late 19th Century - and lots of statues, paintings etc of their heroes Prat, Latorre & Cochrane.  For the 20th century, there was a ginormous model of the Almirante Latorre (1915) - about 40ft long - but not that much more.

The museum shop was quite small, but it sold good quality souvenirs, as well as a range of books on the Chilean Navy - none of which I had ever seen before - I ended up walking out with a superb two volume set on the History of the Chilean Navy - now all I have to do is learn Spanish so I can read it!

Valparaiso isn't the handiest place in the world to get to - but if you ever have a day to spare in Santiago it is a worthwhile visit.
